instruction: Center-align the title 'Dolch Sight Words – Primer' in this document.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to color words in a sight-word table by vowel/consonant using Find & Replace with regex. Used wrong colors (yellow, green instead of red/blue) and also colored paragraph text, not just table words. Replaced 28 vowel-starting and 129 consonant-starting matches across the whole document.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open and navigate LibreOffice Writer, use Find & Replace dialog with regex, open Format dialogs to change font properties, use Replace All for bulk formatting changes.
metadata.failure_analysis: Model used incorrect colors (yellow/green instead of red/blue) and applied formatting to all text, not just table cells. The complex multi-step color assignment task exceeded the model's ability to execute precisely.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to a single alignment change on the title. Model demonstrated ability to interact with the document and use formatting tools. Centering a paragraph is a basic Writer operation.
metadata.explanation: Task requires centering the first paragraph (title). Getter extracts alignment of the first paragraph. Metric checks if alignment equals 'center'. Binary scoring.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts the first paragraph's alignment from the docx file using python-docx, maps alignment enums to readable strings, and defaults None (inherited) alignment to 'left'.

Metric correctly receives the rules dict directly (expected_alignment: 'center') and compares it with the getter's result alignment string. Binary scoring is appropriate for this single-requirement task.
Postconfig properly activates the Writer window and saves the file with Ctrl+S before evaluation, ensuring the getter reads the latest state.
Full instruction coverage: the single requirement (center-align the title) is completely verified by checking paragraph[0] alignment equals 'center'.
Expected parameter handling is correct: metric accesses expected.get('expected_alignment') directly on the rules dict, consistent with the framework's get_rule behavior.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: Getter assumes the title is always paragraphs[0] without verifying the text contains 'Dolch Sight Words'. Consider adding a text check or searching paragraphs for the title text to be more robust.
